subject: Re: Pricing breakdown for audit logs / KMS / on-prem residency (credits & rebate request)
messages:
From: Claire Jensen <claire.jensen@aetherhealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@aetherhealth.com
Date: 2028-03-05T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing breakdown for audit logs / KMS / on-prem residency (credits & rebate request)

Hi Jonas + Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — Aether’s security and platform teams reviewed the capabilities and we have a few follow-ups before procurement will move to an LOI. High level asks: a clear line-itemed price for audit-log retention tiers, KMS/HSM seat vs usage pricing, and options for a hybrid/residency on-prem setup.

Two commercial asks from our side:
- One-time on-prem setup credit (covering professional services & initial infra provisioning) — target range $30k–50k.
- A tiered rebate or per-usage credit that scales down as we ramp (we’d like to see examples for 0–5M tokens/month, 5–20M, 20M+).

Can you provide a short, itemized proposal and whether Redwood can give a pilot concession (reduced HSM seat or waived audit fees) for the first 6 months? I’ve attached a brief summary of our security checklist and target volumes.

Claire Jensen
Sr. Procurement Manager
Aether Health
[Attachment: aether_request_summary.docx (docx)]
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Claire Jensen <claire.jensen@aetherhealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-05T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing breakdown for audit logs / KMS / on-prem residency (credits & rebate request)

Claire — appreciate the clear asks and the checklist. High level proposal attached (PDF) and summarized below so your legal/procurement can quickly map to line items.

Attachment: compliance-pricing-proposal-v1.pdf (pdf)

Summary (short):
- Audit logs: tiered retention pricing (30d / 90d / 365d) with per-GB/month rates; 90d is our most common enterprise default. We propose a 3-month waiver on audit storage for pilots.
- KMS/HSM: two paths — (A) HSM-seats at $X/seat/month (recommended for full customer-managed keys); (B) usage-based envelope encryption charges (lower baseline, variable with encryption ops). We can do a 50% seat discount for the pilot period.
- Data residency / on-prem: engineering setup fee and integration SOW + recurring residency premium (percent of hosted usage). One-time setup effort estimate captured in the SOW. We can trade a portion of the setup fee for a committed volume credit.
- Volume rebate: tiered per-token credit schedule (examples included in the PDF). Rebate structure can be tied to committed throughput or true usage with a lookback reconciliation.

Proposed concessions for a 6-month pilot:
- One-time on-prem setup credit: $35,000 net (applied to first invoice)
- 50% discount on HSM seats for first 6 months (cap of 4 seats)
- Audit log storage waived for first 3 months (up to 5TB)

Next steps: if this direction looks reasonable, I’ll loop Legal to produce a short pilot SOW and a DocuSign-ready addendum. We can also run a 2-week proof-of-concept for the residency connector.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pricing breakdown for audit logs / KMS / on-prem residency (credits & rebate request)

Jonas — thanks for the speedy proposal and the PDF. A few clarifications from procurement and engineering below (quoted for context):

> One-time on-prem setup credit: $35,000 net (applied to first invoice)

We’ll need that credit to cover at least initial provisioning & third-party vendor work — target minimum $40k to be comfortable. Can you move to $40k if we take a 12-month minimal usage commitment?

> 50% discount on HSM seats for first 6 months (cap of 4 seats)

Engineering wants a cap of 6 seats for the pilot (we’ll likely need more for regional redundancy). Could you keep the 50% pilot discount and increase the cap to 6 seats for the first year? After year one we’d revert to standard seat pricing or transition to usage-based keys.

> Audit log storage waived for first 3 months (up to 5TB)

That waiver is useful — procurement asks that any waived amount be documented as a one-time credit line item so our accounting can treat it as non-recurring.

If you can confirm the $40k credit with a 12-month minimum commitment and the pilot seat cap increase, we can draft an LOI and move to SOW review with legal. Also happy to hop on a 30m call to finalize technical acceptance criteria for the PoC.

Claire Jensen
Sr. Procurement Manager, Aether Health
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Claire Jensen <claire.jensen@aetherhealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, contracts@aetherhealth.com
Date: 2028-03-08T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing breakdown for audit logs / KMS / on-prem residency (credits & rebate request)

Claire — we can accomodate the revised asks with the following binding terms for the pilot addendum (we’ll surface in the LOI/SOW):

Committed commercial terms for pilot addendum:
- One-time on-prem setup credit: $40,000 applied as a credit to the first invoice; condition: 12-month minimum usage commitment (standard hosted + residency minimums outlined in SOW).
- HSM seats: 50% discount for first 12 months, capped at 6 seats for the pilot. After 12 months, customers may choose to convert to usage-based key ops pricing or pay standard seat rates.
- Audit logs: storage waived for first 3 months up to 5TB; documented as a one-time credit line item in invoices.
- Volume rebate: we’ll implement a tiered rebate schedule in the contract (examples attached in the PDF). Reconciliation quarterly; credits apply to invoice following the quarter.

Attachments: sow-onprem-pilot.pdf (pdf)
Related links: DocuSign LOI template: https://app.docusign.com/templates/REDWOOD-AE-LOI-2028
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/AE-2028-0311

Ben — please prepare the pilot invoice template reflecting the credit line items so procurement can see the accounting entries.

If that looks good, Claire — let me know a good time for a 30m call tomorrow or Monday to align acceptance criteria.

Best,
Jonas Weber
